title: Banach fixed point from a Cauchy sequence's complete limit
intent: Prove the Banach fixed-point theorem — a contraction T on a complete metric space has a unique fixed point — by naming the limit x of the iterated sequence as the witness and discharging the two obligations of `exists!` (x is fixed, and any two fixed points agree) with two named lemmas, after the sequence's Cauchy property supplies completeness with its certificate.

parent.name: BanachFixedPoint
parent.statement:
Theorem BanachFixedPoint :
    inhabited X ->
    exists! x : X, T x = x.

children.name: BanachFixedPoint_unique
children.statement:
Lemma BanachFixedPoint_unique (x1 x2 : X) :
    T x1 = x1 -> T x2 = x2 -> x1 = x2.

children.name: BanachFixedPoint_seq_cauchy
children.statement:
Local Lemma BanachFixedPoint_seq_cauchy (x : X) :
    cauchy d (BanachFixedPoint_seq x).
children.closed_by: apply BanachFixedPoint_seq_dist_add; ... apply Rle_pow_pos_lt_1; auto (the T x = x case by Nat_iter_fix and metric_zero)

children.name: BanachFixedPoint_seq_limit_fixed

applicability.goal_shape: A unique-existence goal `exists! x : X, T x = x` over a contraction `T : X -> X` on a metric space, where the witness is obtained by a named construction — here the limit of the iterated sequence `BanachFixedPoint_seq x0`, produced by completeness `Hd_comp` from the sequence's Cauchy certificate.
applicability.use_when: The witness comes from a construction that itself needs a certificate (here the Cauchy property), and the two obligations of `exists!` — the candidate satisfies the predicate, and any two satisfying points are equal — are already proved as named lemmas, so the glue only names the witness and splits existence from uniqueness.
applicability.avoid_when: The candidate's required properties are not already factored into separate lemmas (then the glue carries real proof); the uniqueness argument needs a hypothesis the existence argument does not share; or the construction's certificate cannot be stated independently of the witness (here the Cauchy property is stated for the whole sequence before any limit is named).

consequences: The move splits `exists! x : X, T x = x` into two obligations — existence (the witness x is a fixed point) and uniqueness — plus a side certificate: the sequence `BanachFixedPoint_seq x0` must be shown Cauchy before completeness `Hd_comp` yields the witness, and the completeness limit must be converted into a `net_limit` (here by the imported `metric_space_net_limit`) so that `BanachFixedPoint_seq_limit_fixed` applies. Failure modes: if the fixed-point lemma is stated for a `net_limit` while `complete` yields a metric-space limit, the glue must bridge them; if the Cauchy lemma needs a case split (T x = x or not), that split stays inside the child and must not leak into the glue.
